'''Ian Horner Hutchinson''' (7 June 1951) is a nuclear engineer and physicist who is currently Professor of Nuclear Science and Engineering at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. He has made a number of important contributions to the fields of [[nuclear engineering]] and [[nuclear physics]] and has also written about the [[philosophy of science]] and the [[relationship between religion and science]].

==Education and nuclear research==
Hutchinson received his B.A. in physics from [[Cambridge University]] in 1972. He then received his Ph.D. in engineering physics from [[Australian National University]] in 1976, where he was a Commonwealth Scholar.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://web.mit.edu/nse/people/faculty/hutchinson.html | title=Prof Ian Hutchinson, MIT }}</ref>

After receiving his Ph.D. Hutchinson performed experimental research on one of the earliest [[tokamaks]] to be operated outside of the [[Soviet Union]]. He engaged in  further research at [[MIT]] during its first major tokamak research initiative, before doing research for the [[United Kingdom Atomic Energy Authority]]. He returned to MIT in 1983 as a faculty member in the Nuclear Engineering Department, and served as the head of the Department of Nuclear Physics and Engineering from 2003 to 2009.<ref name="psfc">{{Cite web| url=http://www.psfc.mit.edu/~hutch/hutchbio.html | title=Prof. Ian H. Hutchinson | access-date=2012-06-11 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910205504/http://www.psfc.mit.edu/~hutch/hutchbio.html | archive-date=2015-09-10 | url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hutchinson has authored more than 160 journal articles on plasma phenomena and [[nuclear fusion]]. He was the 2008 chairman of the Division of Plasma Physics group of the [[American Physical Society]], of which he had been elected a fellow in 1988.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1988&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate= 27 September 2020}}</ref> He is author of the standard monograph on measuring plasmas, ''Principles of Plasma Diagnostics''.

==Science and religion==
Hutchinson has authored a book on the philosophy of science, arguing against [[scientism]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://biologos.org/blog/monopolizing-knowledge-part-1-science-and-scientism |title=Monopolizing Knowledge, Part 1: Science and Scientism &#124; the BioLogos Forum |access-date=2012-06-11 |archive-date=2015-04-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427162736/http://biologos.org/blog/monopolizing-knowledge-part-1-science-and-scientism |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | title=Ian Hutchinson's Web Site | url=http://monopolizingknowledge.net/ | access-date=2026-02-17 | website=monopolizingknowledge.net}}</ref> Hutchinson is a contributor to the [[BioLogos Foundation]] and has written and spoken on the [[relationship between science and religion]], arguing that religious belief, and belief in [[Christianity]] in particular, can be perfectly reconciled with science.<ref>{{Cite web| url=http://biologos.org/uploads/projects/hutchinson_white_paper.pdf | title=Engaging Today's Militant Atheist Arguments | access-date=2012-06-11 | archive-date=2012-06-11 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120611001106/http://biologos.org/uploads/projects/hutchinson_white_paper.pdf | url-status=dead}}</ref> He has spoken at the [[Veritas Forum]] on the topic of miracles, debating atheist philosophy professor [[Donald Hubin]].<ref>The Veritas Forum, [http://www.veritas.org/miracles-an-osu-atheist-and-an-mit-christian-discuss-belief-and-reason/ ''Miracles: an OSU Atheist and an MIT Christian discuss belief and reason''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017031352/http://www.veritas.org/miracles-an-osu-atheist-and-an-mit-christian-discuss-belief-and-reason/ |date=2017-10-17 }}, 2015.</ref><ref>{{cite AV media| url-status = live| archive-url = https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211209/BHFmYbznPZw| archive-date = 2021-12-09| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BHFmYbznPZw| title = Science and Faith? Ian Hutchinson explains how the two fit together. | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He has also argued against [[New Atheism]].<ref>Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211209/nrqY2aG4GE4 Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20121129104706/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nrqY2aG4GE4&gl=US&hl=en Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{cite AV media| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nrqY2aG4GE4| title = Science and Scientism - Ian Hutchinson at MIT | website=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://biologos.org/blog/ian-hutchinson-on-the-new-atheists |title=Ian Hutchinson on the New Atheists &#124; BioLogos |access-date=2012-06-11 |archive-date=2012-04-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120424025540/http://biologos.org/blog/ian-hutchinson-on-the-new-atheists |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==TtH==
Hutchinson is the author of the computer program TtH, a [[TeX]] to [[HTML]] translator, a popular program for web-publishing of mathematics.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://aminet.net/package/text/tex/TtH | title=Aminet - text/Tex/TTH.lha }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.trevorrow.com/oztex/ | title=OzTeX }}</ref>
